title: A particle speeds up and then slows down
stem: A particle has velocity $v(t)=4te^{-t^2}$ m s$^{-1}$ for $t\ge0$.

title: Area between exponential mirror graphs
stem: Consider $y=e^x$ and $y=e^{-x}$ between the vertical lines $x=-\ln2$ and $x=\ln2$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find their intersection and state which graph is upper on each side.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the total area between the curves exactly.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why a single signed integral of eˣ−e⁻ˣ over the whole interval is zero.

steps.text: Intersection $(0,1)$; $e^{-x}$ upper for x<0 and $e^x$ upper for x>0.
Reflection symmetry gives twice the positive-side area.
The difference is odd and the interval is symmetric, so opposite signed contributions cancel although geometric area is positive.

answerSummary: Intersection $(0,1)$; total area 1; signed whole-interval difference integral 0.
